content:
**June — Juneau, Alaska**

Juneau is the only U.S. state capital on the Pacific coast that receives more rainfall than any of the other Pacific‑bordering capitals. Its average annual precipitation is roughly **93 inches (≈ 2 360 mm) per year**, far exceeding the amounts recorded in:

| Capital | State | Avg. annual precipitation |
|---------|-------|----------------------------|
| Sacramento | California | ~20 in (≈ 520 mm) |
| Salem | Oregon | ~45 in (≈ 1 140 mm) |
| Olympia | Washington | ~55 in (≈ 1 400 mm) |
| Honolulu | Hawaii | ~17 in (≈ 430 mm) |
| **Juneau** | **Alaska** | **≈ 93 in (≈ 2 360 mm)** |

Juneau sits on the Gastineau Channel, an arm of the Inside Passage that opens onto the Pacific Ocean, and its coastal maritime climate brings abundant moisture year‑round, making it the rainiest of the Pacific‑bordering state capitals.
